newsitem.title: CANADA: W. CANADA GRAIN WILTS UNDER HEAT, DISEASE-CWB.
newsitem.headline: W. CANADA GRAIN WILTS UNDER HEAT, DISEASE-CWB.

text.p: Western Canadian cereal crop yields were forecast to fall below the 10-year average due to drought stress and fusarium head blight, Canadian Wheat Board officials told an industry briefing here.
All wheat production in western Canada was expected to be 21.6 million tonnes, CWB chief commissioner Lorne Hehn said.
Statistics Canada's last estimate, issued June 27 and based on a May survey of farmers, pegged output at 21.955 million tonnes.
Chicago Board of Trade December wheat futures ended up 3/4 of a U.S. cent a bushel at US$3.77-3/4, in part on the CWB's cut in western Canadian production prospects.
Prairie milling wheat yields were expected to reach 28.5 bushels an acre compared to the 10-year average of 31.5 bu/ac, CWB weather and crop surveillance director Paul Bullock said.
Durum wheat yields were seen at 26.5 bu/ac compared to the 10-year average of 30 bu/ac, he said.
Barley yields were forecast at 55.3 bu/ac versus the 56 bu/ac trend, he added.

"There's probably more downside than upside but at this point there's probably not going to be any major changes, we don't think rainfall's going to make much of a difference in terms of improving things," Bullock said.
Hot, dry weather in southeast Alberta, south Saskatchewan and southwest Manitoba cut yields, CWB's Hehn said.
"I have some concern about the incidence of fusarium head blight (scab) and it's always a hard one to read but there's no question there's going to be some yield reduction as a result," Hehn added.
